opening.headline: We solve the difficult problem of how to insert 30 pages of an in-house manual into the assistant by dividing the manual into rules, materials, and practices.
body: The customer service team's return processing manual is 30 pages long. It's a jumble of procedures, exceptions, forms, and contact information. If you paste all of this document into the instructions box, the instructions will be long and blurry and the rules will be ignored. If you upload it as a file, it will only be used as a reference, not as a judgment rule. Action-requiring issues, such as issuing refunds, cannot be resolved through instructions or files.

In this class, you will learn the principle of dividing a manual into three parts: instructions, knowledge, tools, and authority. We then look at how to transfer procedures and exceptions into the structure of situations and actions, and how to place human checkpoints before execution. At the end, we solve an example of converting the return processing manual into an assistant configuration and determining whether the result is complete.

As of 2026-10: Gems are transitioning to skills. Personal accounts will be converted after November 2026, and Workspace business accounts will be converted after March 2027. The Gems screen below is based on the pre-migration environment. After moving the instructions and files, please check again for sharing and tool operation.

screens.title: I don't know how to put 30 pages of the in-house manual into the assistant.
screens.lead:
First, let's look at the problems that arise when the manual is inserted as is. Read on to see why each of the three attempts fell short.

As of 2026-10: Gems are transitioning to skills. Personal accounts will be converted after November 2026, and Workspace business accounts will be converted after March 2027. The Gems screen below is based on the pre-migration environment. After moving the instructions and files, please check again for sharing and tool operation.

visual.alt: A 30-page manual bundle on the left and three empty assistant configuration screens on the right.

paragraphs: The customer service team's returns processing manual is 30 pages long and a jumble of procedures, exceptions, forms, and contact information. I would like to add this manual to my assistant to handle return inquiries.

Your first attempt is to paste everything into the instructions box. The instructions are long and blurry and the rules are ignored. My second attempt is to upload it as a file only. The file is used as reference material only and does not determine how the decision will be made. Third, things that require action, such as issuing refunds, cannot be accomplished with instructions or files.
The question for this class is this. Which parts of the manual should go to guidance, which parts should go to knowledge, and which parts should go to authority?

screens.outro: First, let's think about how to use the manual.

screens.title: What parts of the manual are actually used for judgment?
screens.lead: When you select each question, the instructor's thoughts unfold. You will not enter or submit your answer, so think first before clicking.

items.prompt: Where does a new person actually open the manual?
items.answer: There is usually a page explaining the judgment order and a page with a table or form. Read the speaking guide and outline once and move on. This shows that the contents of the manual are being used in different ways.

items.prompt: Are there any parts of the manual you've never read?
items.answer: If so, it is likely that it is not a rule that is always needed, but rather material that is only looked for in specific situations or content that is already familiar. Leaving these parts in the body of the guidance obscures the core rules.

items.prompt: Are the reading part, the following part, and the directly executing part the same?
items.answer: It's different. What you read and refer to are materials, what you follow are rules, and what you directly process in the system is execution. These three correspond to the assistant's knowledge, instructions, tools, and authority respectively.

screens.outro: Now that we've established that the three are different, let's look at how to divide the manual.

screens.title: Breakdown of the Manual: Rules, Materials, Practices
screens.lead: Select the highlighted sentences one by one from the manual excerpt below. An explanation appears as to whether the sentence goes to instructions, knowledge, tools, or authority.

visual.alt: A schematic where one page of the manual is divided by three arrows and goes into three boxes.
labels: Guidelines: Rules (how to judge and speak)
Tools and Permissions: Run (Working with the System)

data.text:
[Excerpt from Return Processing Manual]
Always respond to customers with polite respect.
When a return request is made, the date of purchase and product condition are first checked before determining whether a return is possible.
Return deadlines for each item follow the attached table.
The return application must be completed according to the attached form.
The system registers a refund request and sends a return label.
Refunds exceeding 100,000 won will be processed after approval from the team leader.

marks.span: Always respond to customers with polite respect.
marks.note: These are the rules that determine how to say things, so they go as guidelines. Rules are what determines how to judge and speak. GPT guidance also tells you to write down the rules, tone, and workflow in the instructions.

marks.span: When a return request is made, the date of purchase and product condition are first checked before determining whether a return is possible.
marks.note: Since this is a procedure that determines the order of judgment, we go to the guidelines. When a situation arises, I write it down in the form of acting like this.

marks.span: Return deadlines for each item follow the attached table.
marks.note: This is the source material to look for. The table is long and may change as the number of items increases, so go to the knowledge file. The instructions only provide the proviso that return deadlines follow the table in the knowledge file.

marks.span: The return application must be completed according to the attached form.
marks.note: The form is a reference, so it goes to knowledge. However, the rules for how to fill out the application form are placed in the instructions, and the original form is placed in the knowledge section.

marks.span: The system registers a refund request and sends a return label.
marks.note: An execution that does work on an external system. You can't do this with instructions or files, so go to Tools and Permissions Settings.

marks.span: Refunds exceeding 100,000 won will be processed after approval from the team leader.
marks.note: It is a verification point that must be checked by a human before execution. Rules that require approval are written in the instructions, and the tool also includes requests for approval or restrictions on execution permissions.

screens.outro: Now that we've identified the differences between the three branches, let's take a closer look at the boundaries between guidance and knowledge.

screens.title: Distinction between guidelines and knowledge: Rules are guidelines, long and changing evidence is knowledge
screens.lead: Use the switch to switch between instructions and knowledge, and compare how the response changes when the same manual item is placed on either side.

states.label: instructions
states.body: Guidelines are a set of rules that apply to every conversation. There are certain things that must always be the same, such as the order in which we determine whether a return is possible or how we respond. Putting the entire return deadline table in your instructions will make the instructions longer, obscure the core rules, and require you to revise the instructions every time the table changes. The ChatGPT project has instructions and files together, and the Claude project's instructions are used for all chats in the project. The same distinction exists in Gems. The instructions include rules and information about when and how to consult knowledge files. Only then will the guidance and knowledge be linked together and operate as a single construct.

states.label: knowledge
states.body: Knowledge is a resource that can be found and used when needed. GPT guidance describes knowledge as appropriate for reference materials such as documents, guides, and handbooks. This includes an item-specific return deadline table or example form. If rules are written in a knowledge file, the judgment method may remain reference-based and not always applicable. If you wish to cite an uploaded file, you must specify the method and format in the instructions. Gem can upload knowledge files, and Drive files reflect the most recent version. The Claude project has separate knowledge and instructions.

screens.outro: Now that we have identified the boundaries, let's look at how to move procedures, exceptions, and checkpoints into the structure.

screens.title: Moving procedures, exceptions, and checkpoints into structures
screens.lead: Click the Next Step button to follow the procedure in the manual, with exception branches and checkpoints added one after the other.

visual.alt: Schematic of one line of procedure flow with exception branches and human check marks.
labels: Check purchase date and product status
Expired or Opened: Following the Table of Knowledge

steps.title: A procedure is a pair of situations and actions.
steps.body: The procedures in the manual are sequential steps. This is written in the form of action in situations in the guidelines. For example, when a return request is made, we first check the purchase date and product condition, and then determine whether a return is possible. Numbering the order makes it clear which step comes first.

steps.title: Exceptions are conditional branches
steps.body: Exceptions are conditions attached to a procedure. A conditional branch is used to describe what to do if the product has been opened or its expiration date has passed. Since the instructions become long when there are more than two or three exceptions, many exceptions can be moved to a table in the knowledge file, with the only exception being left in the instructions with the caveat that the exceptions follow the table.

steps.title: Mark confirmation points
steps.body: A verification point is where human confirmation is required before execution. An example is the rule that refunds over 100,000 won are processed only after approval from the team leader. The instructions clearly state under what conditions you will stop and hand it over to the person.

steps.title: Support verification points with authority
steps.body: Guidance alone may not be enough to stop a run, so we're betting on the tools too. ChatGPT informs you that apps may ask for permission before browsing or doing things outside of your home. Claude explains that you can restrict execution permissions on a per-service basis, such as allowing only reads and preventing writes. Putting rules and permissions together makes verification points really work.

screens.outro: Now that we have learned the structure, let’s look at an example of dividing an actual manual.

screens.title: Commentary: Divide the returns processing manual into instructions, knowledge, and authority.
screens.lead: Click the Next Step button to follow the instructor as he moves the twelve items in the manual's table of contents to three positions.

steps.title: Look through the table of contents
steps.body: There are twelve items in the table of contents of the Returns Processing Manual. The instructor first asks each item whether it is a rule, material, or practice. If an item contains two personalities, split it up and send each to its appropriate place.

steps.title: Points to Instructions
steps.body: The tone of customer service and the order in which a return is possible are determined as guidelines. Both are rules that should be the same in all returns conversations. The decision order is written in numbered steps, and the speech is abbreviated to two lines.

steps.title: Entry to Knowledge
steps.body: Tables of return deadlines for each item and example return forms are available in the knowledge file. It's a long and subject-matter of evidence. The instructions leave only one line: return deadlines follow the table in the knowledge file.

steps.title: Go to Tools and Permissions
steps.body: Registering a refund request and sending a return label are actions that work in the system, so go to Connecting Tools and Setting Permissions. Instructions or files are not a substitute for execution.

steps.title: Have a checkpoint
steps.body: We note in the instructions that large refunds are a verification point that requires human verification. If it is over 100,000 won, it is a sentence that tells you not to process it and to request approval from the team leader. The tool also requests approval or restricts execution permissions.

steps.title: result
steps.body: Twelve items organized into one sheet of instructions, two knowledge files, one connection tool, and one checkpoint. The 30-page manual is divided into short instructions, reference material when needed, and controlled practice.

screens.outro: Now that we have the configuration, let's look at some checking questions to determine if this transformation is complete.

screens.title: Explanation: Determine whether the conversion result is complete
screens.lead: As you select each inspection question, you'll see how the case met it and the risks of missing it. Please judge for yourself first and then press it.

items.prompt: Check 1: Are all items in the manual in one of the three positions?
items.answer: In our case, all twelve items went to one of the following: Guidelines, Knowledge, Tools and Powers. If an item doesn't go anywhere, it becomes a rule that the assistant doesn't know about, and human work is quietly missed. Items such as contact information and escalation paths are especially frequently omitted from the manual, so it is safer to check the table of contents line by line.

items.prompt: Check 2: Are there procedures and exception handling standards in the guidelines?
items.answer: The guidelines have a numbered order of judgment, and exceptions follow the table of knowledge. If there is no order, returns may be approved without confirming the date of purchase, and if there are no exception criteria, the response will vary depending on the exception situation.

items.prompt: Check 3: Are there checkpoints or permission restrictions at each execution stage?
items.answer: When registering a refund request, there is a confirmation point of team leader approval when the amount is over 100,000 won, and the tool has approval requests and permission restrictions. If this is missing, there is a risk that large refunds will be processed without human verification.

items.prompt: Check 4: Are knowledge files linked with clues on when to refer to them?
items.answer: There is a proviso in the instructions that return deadlines follow the table in the knowledge file. Without a clue, the Assistant may not utilize it even if the file is up. The GPT instructions instruct you to upload the file and then check whether it is being used as intended in Preview. Uploading a knowledge file and making it usable are two different things, so keep in mind the connection clue and preview confirmation as a pair.

screens.outro: Now that we've completed the four checks, let's summarize the key points.

screens.title: Key takeaways
screens.lead: Summarizes the contents of this class. As you read, try to answer the initial question: Which part of the manual goes where?

paragraphs: The initial question was which part of the manual goes where: guidance, knowledge, or authority. Rules belong to instructions, materials to knowledge, and execution to tools and authority. Guidelines determine how to judge and speak, knowledge determines what to base things on, and tools determine how to work in the system.

Procedures are written in the form of actions for situations, and written as conditions for exceptions. If there are a lot of exceptions, move them to knowledge and leave only clues in the instructions. In the execution phase, we place verification points and permission restrictions so that humans stop where they need to check.

Once the conversion is done, check that everything is somewhere, that the instructions have order and exception criteria, that the execution has checkpoints, that the knowledge file has reference clues, and that it's actually being used as a preview.

Think back to the manual on page 30 of the first scene. Now, instead of asking where to paste this manual, is this sentence a rule, data, or practice? This one question is the starting point for turning manuals into assistant configurations in the same way, whether in projects in ChatGPT, GPT, Claude projects, or Gem. After dividing the items, check whether the instructions have been shortened and whether the clues are connected to the knowledge.

callout.label: Points to remember
callout.text: Uploading the entire manual is not a conversion. Only when you determine whether each item is a rule, data, or execution and place it in the appropriate location will the assistant work according to the manual.

glossary.def: The task is to divide the document into rules, data, and practices and place each in its appropriate place.
The principle is that how to make a judgment is based on guidelines and what to base it on is based on knowledge.
It refers to sequential steps and conditional branches attached to those steps.
This step involves human confirmation before execution. Write it down in the instructions and support it with tool approvals or permission restrictions.

misconceptions.myth: The manual can be uploaded in its entirety.
misconceptions.fact: If you put it in its entirety in the instructions, the rules will become unclear, and if you upload it as a file, it will only be used as reference material. To be used properly, rules must be divided into guidelines, data into knowledge, and execution into authority.

misconceptions.myth: Even if rules are written in a knowledge file, they are the same as guidelines.
misconceptions.fact: Like the GPT guide, the knowledge is for reference, and rules such as tone and workflow are left in the instructions.

misconceptions.myth: If you upload a file, the assistant can take action.
misconceptions.fact: Execution is the realm of tool association and permission setting. A file is just readable data.

closing.lead: Summarizes what was covered in this class.
points: Rules are divided into guidelines, materials are knowledge, and execution is divided into authority.
Procedures are written as pairs of situations and actions, and exceptions are written as conditions.
The execution phase places verification points and permission restrictions.
After conversion, make sure everything is somewhere and available in Preview.

checks.q: Match where to place the contents of the returns processing manual
left: Customer response tone and order of decision whether return is possible or not
Return deadline table for each item
checks.explain: Rules such as how to make decisions and how to speak go as guidelines, reference materials to look for as knowledge, and execution of work in external systems go as tools and authority.
checks.intro: Check for yourself what you just learned. Results are not recorded.

checks.q: What is the best way to prevent the returns assistant from immediately processing large refunds without human verification?
options: Upload the refund deadline table once again as a knowledge file
Increase guidelines for refund language to be more polite
For each large refund request, open a new conversation and explain it from the beginning.
Write down large refunds in instructions as a confirmation point that requires human verification and limit execution authority.
checks.explain: Places that require human confirmation before execution are written in the instructions as confirmation points, and on the tool side, permission restrictions such as requesting approval or read-only are applied.

wrong.0: The deadline table is only a basis for judgment and is not a device to stop execution.
wrong.1: The tone of speech has nothing to do with whether it is processed or not.
wrong.2: Explaining things in each conversation neither sustains the rules nor prevents their implementation.
